The Vision of Reality.

In Sanskrit, philosophy is called Darshana—not just a love of wisdom, but a direct "vision" of the Truth.

The Six Orthodox Schools (Shad Darshanas) form the intellectual bedrock of Sanatan Dharma. While they range from strict logic to absolute non-dualism, all six are soteriological: they exist for the sole purpose of ending human suffering and achieving Moksha.

Vedanta

The culmination of Vedic wisdom exploring the nature of ultimate reality and the self.

Key Question

"What is ultimately real?"

Advaita Vedanta

Non-dual philosophy teaching that individual self and universal consciousness are one.

Key Question

"Who am I, really?"

Vishishtadvaita

Qualified non-dualism seeing God, souls, and world as distinct yet inseparable.

Key Question

"How do I relate to the Divine?"

Dvaita

Dualist philosophy emphasizing eternal distinction between God, souls, and matter.

Key Question

"How do I serve the Divine?"

Samkhya

Ancient analytical philosophy distinguishing pure consciousness from material nature.

Key Question

"What is the structure of existence?"

Yoga Darshana

Patanjali's systematic path of mental discipline leading to liberation.

Key Question

"How do I still the mind?"

Mimamsa

Philosophy of Vedic ritual, duty, and the power of sacred action.

Key Question

"What is my sacred duty?"

Nyaya-Vaisheshika

Schools of logic, epistemology, and atomic theory seeking truth through reason.

Key Question

"How do I know what is true?"

Comparative Logic

Deep analysis of how these systems intersect, conflict, and complement one another.
